sources.openapi: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/oas/v2 (YAML); schema/openapi.pinned.json is the pinned subset the weekly drift check compares
sources.metadata: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/metadata: every curated ctgov.fields.* path is verified to exist there; the endpoint and field text is curated by hand

endpoints.description: Search studies (GET /studies) by condition, intervention, location, sponsor or free text, with status and geo filters. Parameters are FLAT dotted string keys, never nested objects: 'query.cond', 'query.term', 'query.intr', 'query.locn', 'query.spons', 'query.lead', 'filter.overallStatus' (array of status enums), 'filter.geo', 'filter.advanced' (Essie expression); plus fields, sort, countTotal, pageSize (0-1000) and pageToken. See ctgov.syntax.search, ctgov.syntax.essie, ctgov.syntax.geo and ctgov.syntax.paging. Returns { studies: [...], nextPageToken?, totalCount? }. Always pass fields: full study records are large and a result over 256 KiB fails.
endpoints.example: const page = await ctgov.studies.search({ 'query.cond': 'lung cancer', 'filter.overallStatus': ['RECRUITING'], fields: ['NCTId', 'BriefTitle', 'Phase'], pageSize: 20, countTotal: true }); return { total: page.totalCount, studies: page.studies.map(s => s.protocolSection.identificationModule) }

endpoints.description: One study by NCT ID (GET /studies/{nctId}); nctId must match NCT followed by 8 digits. fields projects the record (piece names or dotted module names). format is 'json' (default, parsed), 'csv', 'fhir.json' or 'ris'; csv and ris come back as raw text. Returns the study object ({ protocolSection, resultsSection?, derivedSection?, hasResults }).
endpoints.example: const s = await ctgov.studies.get('NCT04852770', { fields: ['NCTId', 'BriefTitle', 'OverallStatus', 'EligibilityCriteria'] }); return s.protocolSection

endpoints.description: The study data model (GET /studies/metadata): a tree of field nodes with name, piece (the name to use in fields), type, sourceType and children. Large; filter it in the sandbox and return only the matching nodes. Use describe_schema for the curated field list first.
endpoints.example: const tree = await ctgov.studies.metadata(); return tree.map(n => ({ name: n.name, piece: n.piece, children: (n.children ?? []).length }))

endpoints.description: The search areas (GET /studies/search-areas): [{ name: 'Study', areas: [{ name (BasicSearch, ConditionSearch, ...), param (the query.* key it backs), parts: [{ pieces, weight }] }] }]. Useful for choosing the area names in an Essie AREA[...] expression and the query.* key that searches a given field set.
endpoints.example: const [study] = await ctgov.studies.searchAreas(); return study.areas.map(a => ({ area: a.name, param: a.param }))

endpoints.description: All enumeration types and their values (GET /studies/enums), e.g. Status, Phase, StudyType. Use it to spell filter.overallStatus values and phase names exactly.
endpoints.example: const enums = await ctgov.studies.enums(); return enums.find(x => x.type === 'Status')

endpoints.description: Size statistics of the whole database (GET /stats/size): { totalStudies, averageSizeBytes, ranges[] }.

Value distribution of one or more fields across all studies (GET /stats/field/values): for enum fields the count per value (e.g. OverallStatus, Phase), for others missing and distinct counts. fields is required and non-empty; types optionally limits to ENUM, STRING, DATE, INTEGER, NUMBER, BOOLEAN.
endpoints.example: const stats = await ctgov.stats.fieldValues({ fields: ['OverallStatus'] }); return stats[0].topValues

endpoints.description: Size statistics of array fields across all studies (GET /stats/field/sizes): min, max and a histogram of list lengths, e.g. for Phase, Condition or LocationFacility. fields is required and non-empty.
endpoints.example: const sizes = await ctgov.stats.fieldSizes({ fields: ['Condition'] }); return sizes[0]

endpoints.description: API and data timestamp versions (GET /version): { apiVersion, dataTimestamp }. Cheap health check and a way to cite the data snapshot.

fields.description: Query syntax of ctgov.studies.search. Flat dotted string keys (never nested objects): 'query.cond', 'query.term', 'query.intr', 'query.locn', 'query.spons', 'query.lead', 'query.titles', 'query.outc', 'query.id', 'query.patient' take natural text or Essie expressions (AND, OR, NOT, quotes, parentheses); 'filter.overallStatus' and 'postFilter.overallStatus' take enum arrays; 'filter.ids' takes NCT ids; 'filter.advanced' takes an Essie expression; sort takes 'FieldName:asc|desc' or '@relevance'. Unknown keys are rejected with a ValidationError.

Essie expressions (filter.advanced and the query.* fields) address a search area or field with AREA[Name]: 'AREA[Phase]PHASE3', numeric and date ranges 'AREA[StartDate]RANGE[2020-01-01, MAX]' (MIN and MAX are open ends), 'AREA[EnrollmentCount]RANGE[100, 500]', and boolean combinations 'AREA[LeadSponsorClass]INDUSTRY AND AREA[StudyType]INTERVENTIONAL'. Use ctgov.studies.searchAreas() for area names and ctgov.studies.enums() for enum values.
fields.example: await ctgov.studies.search({ 'filter.advanced': 'AREA[StartDate]RANGE[2024-01-01, MAX] AND AREA[Phase]PHASE3', fields: ['NCTId', 'StartDate'], pageSize: 5 })

fields.description: filter.geo restricts studies to those with a site within a radius: 'distance(latitude,longitude,radius)' with the radius as a number plus mi or km, e.g. 'distance(42.36,-71.06,50mi)'. A matching study still lists ALL its sites in LocationFacility/LocationGeoPoint: filter the locations in the sandbox (haversine on geoPoint.lat/lon) to get the nearest ones. geoDecay ('func:linear,scale:100mi,offset:10mi,decay:0.5') boosts nearer sites when sorting by relevance.

Paging: each studies.search call returns one page of at most pageSize studies (0-1000, default 10) and, when more remain, nextPageToken. Pass it back as pageToken with the SAME other parameters to get the next page; stop when nextPageToken is missing. countTotal: true adds totalCount (send it on the first page only). There is no searchAll helper: loop with a bounded page count, since every page is one call against the per-execute budget.
fields.example: const out = []; let pageToken; for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) { const page = await ctgov.studies.search({ 'query.cond': 'melanoma', fields: ['NCTId'], pageSize: 100, ...(pageToken ? { pageToken } : {}) }); out.push(...page.studies.map(s => s.protocolSection.identificationModule.nctId)); pageToken = page.nextPageToken; if (!pageToken) break; } return out

fields.description: Projection: pass fields on studies.search and studies.get to cut the response to what you need (a full study record can be hundreds of KiB and an execute result over 256 KiB fails). Use piece names (NCTId, BriefTitle, OverallStatus, Phase, EnrollmentCount, LeadSponsorName, Condition, InterventionName, EligibilityCriteria, LocationFacility, LocationCity, LocationGeoPoint, ...); ctgov.studies.metadata() lists them. The response keeps the nested protocolSection/derivedSection/resultsSection shape, containing only those fields.
NCT identifiers are 'NCT' followed by 8 digits ('NCT04852770'). studies.get rejects anything else with a ValidationError. filter.ids takes an array of them and 'query.id' searches secondary ids too.

SDK errors keep name, message and status inside the sandbox: ValidationError (bad arguments; never sent upstream), NotFound (404), BadRequest (400, with the upstream reason), RateLimited (429 or this server's request queue is full), UpstreamTimeout, UpstreamUnavailable, HttpError (any other upstream status of 400 or above, including 5xx), ResponseTooLarge (the upstream body exceeded the response cap: use a smaller pageSize or fields), CallBudgetExceeded, SubjectQuotaExceeded, QuotaUnavailable (the hourly quota could not be checked). Catch them with try/catch and inspect e.name and e.status.
Short study title shown in listings. (string)
Overall status: RECRUITING, COMPLETED, TERMINATED, etc. (enum)
Phase list: PHASE1, PHASE2, PHASE3, PHASE4, EARLY_PHASE1, NA. (enum[])
Inclusion and exclusion criteria in markdown. (markdown)
Facility and geo info for each site (facility, city, state, country, geoPoint). (array)
MeSH terms mapped from declared conditions. (array)
MeSH terms mapped from declared interventions. (array)
Serious and other adverse events (only when hasResults). (object)
True if the study has posted results. (boolean)
